Consolidated P2: final highlights

Advance the frozen consolidated selector as the first policy for maintainer review, not as a proven universal optimum. Retain one common K1 queue, the shared large-input caps, and conservative small-parallel guards; do not route permanently among v1/v2/v3 or refit thresholds from this matrix. The held-out results retain the large complete-call gains with no predeclared material regression flags. Production adoption still requires discussing the recurring ~0.079ms first-call scheduler tradeoff and accepting deliberately missed streaming gains for enlarged tables. The strict L==isqrt(x) gate is intentionally conservative and has a visible performance discontinuity for 0.1% enlargement; it is an empirical safety boundary, not a mathematical crossover. No retuning or production edits were made.

12,104 timed counts matched (8,840 focus;3,264 held-out), 3,026 fresh processes. Candidate frozen before focus and held-out runs. Focus:1 predeclared flag;held-out:0.

Measured vector capacities only, not RSS. Conservative scratch peak accounts for sequential Phi/stream phases; excludes thread stacks, allocator overhead, shared Phi cache and other process allocations.

Displayed timings are medians of process medians. Changes are medians of paired block ratios/differences; they need not equal ratios/differences of displayed medians. Every-block direction is descriptive, not a statistical significance claim.

All18 focused complete-call cases select identical partitions and worker budgets in v2,v3,andcandidate. Their differing within5% first-call counts cannot establish a dispatch advantage.
